objective: Official, point-in-time expense ratios for the model universe from the SEC Mutual Fund Prospectus Risk/Return Summary data sets, matched by SEC class ID.

matching.not_covered: Unit investment trusts (e.g. SPY, DIA), grantor trusts (e.g. GLD, IBIT), commodity pools and ETNs do not file risk/return summaries; their cost stays UNKNOWN, never imputed.

point_in_time: a fund's expense ratio at a date is the one in its latest filing filed on or before that date

changes: A published quarter that parses to 0 class filings raises a GitHub warning with diagnostics (expense facts in the archive, facts without a class, facts with other dimensions, taxonomy versions), is downloaded again once in case the cached archive is stale, and is listed in expense_ratio_summary.json (empty_published_quarters, diagnostics, newest_filing). The package carries a limitation while recent quarters are empty.

A fact whose class column is empty but whose only dimension names one SEC class ID is read as that class (the open-end fund taxonomy places the share class in a dimension). Untested against live SEC data from this sandbox: the diagnostics of the next run show whether it applies.
amendments.finding: Quarters 2025q3-2026q2 parsed 0 rows and 2025q2 has no filings after 2025-05-12 (other years have about 50 June filings). The stop falls mid-quarter, so it is not a URL pattern (that would be NOT_PUBLISHED) or a cache artifact (the archives were first downloaded on 2026-10-07). The likely cause is a change in how the filings are tagged from about May 2025, consistent with the SEC's move of risk/return data into the open-end fund (OEF) taxonomy, where the parser's filters (class column required, no other dimensions) drop every fact.
